spec.description: The function renders a complete frame onto the provided canvas context, using the fields of the renderState object. It first fills the entire canvas with a sky color derived from the current time-of-day (interpolating between predefined dawn, day, dusk, and night colors). If it is not daytime, a set of star points is drawn; each star’s position follows a deterministic pattern that includes a parallax offset from the camera, and its opacity oscillates over time based on the tick counter. A sun circle (for daytime) or moon circle (otherwise) is then drawn, its location determined by the fraction of the daily cycle. Tiles from the world grid that lie within the camera viewport are drawn as colored rectangles of a constant grid size; grass, torch, and chest tiles receive additional graphical markings, and ore tiles have a random chance per frame to show a few small bright specks. Each enemy is rendered according to its type definition: slimes as ellipses, flyers as rectangles with flapping side attachments, and walkers as plain rectangles; if an enemy is damaged, a health bar is drawn above it. The player character is drawn with a yellow body, head, brown boots, white eyes, and—if an immunity timer is active—the player’s alpha is toggled to create a blinking effect; when the player holds a sword item and the attack cooldown is above a threshold, an arc indicating a swing is drawn. All active particles are rendered at their positions with alpha proportional to remaining life. If the left mouse button is held, the targeted tile (if within a bounded range and active) is outlined in yellow. Finally, a heads‑up display is drawn: a health bar at the bottom‑left (fixed pixel width, colored green/yellow/red according to the health fraction and labeled with current and maximum hp), a text showing the day number and whether it is day or night at the top‑right, and a hotbar at the bottom‑center. The hotbar contains a fixed number of inventory slots; the active slot is highlighted with a gold border, and each slot displays a truncated item name and stack count. A coin counter is drawn near the health bar. Throughout the rendering, the global alpha is temporarily modified for stars and certain entity effects and is reset to full opacity after each group.
